results.content:
Missed the push? Pushary can call you, by default within a minute of the push, and read the request. You approve it, say no or tell the agent what to do. Calls need a confirmed phone number and work in English, German, French and Dutch. Calls cover Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Hermes and the other agents listed on the calls page, not yet Cursor, VS Code, OpenCode or OpenClaw. Set it up with `npx -y pushary@latest calls`. Phone calls · How calls work

If your agent runs in front of you and you only need to know when it finishes, you do not need any of the above and you should not pay for it:

`npx -y pushary@latest bell` [...] `npx -y pushary@latest bell`

That is the whole thing. It makes a noise in your terminal and raises a desktop notification when Claude Code says an agent finished or is waiting on you. It rides Claude Code's own notification events, so it fires when you have actually stepped away rather than after every reply. No account, no API key, no network call, nothing leaves your machine. Turn it off with `npx -y pushary@latest bell --off`; it touches nothing else in your settings.

You probably ran this, from a blog post or an answer somewhere:

`claude config set --global preferrednotifchannel terminal_bell error: unknown option '--global'`

`claude config set` no longer takes `--global`. The setting moved into `~/.claude/settings.json`, so the direct equivalent is to put it there yourself: [...] You step away while Claude Code runs the tests. It finishes and asks whether to open a pull request. Pushary sends the question to your phone. If you miss the push and have calls enabled, Pushary can ring you and read the question aloud. Say “show me the test results first” and Claude gets your answer in the session you left running.

`npx -y pushary@latest setup`

Setup connects the tools and approval hooks your agent supports. Keep the computer running and take the agent’s question on your phone when you step away.

There are three things.

Notify. The agent sends a push when a long task finishes or when a build, test, or deploy fails. The notification can carry what changed, the error, and suggested next steps.

results.title: Troubleshooting | Pushary Agent Docs
results.content:
# Troubleshooting

Fix Pushary agent notifications that do not arrive. What to do when your phone does not buzz, the agent does not ask, or doctor reports a failed check.

Updated

Most problems with agent notifications come down to three things: no phone is paired, the agent's hook is not running, or a rule decided the call without asking you. Each section below starts with the fix, then the reasons behind it. Start by running the health check on the machine where your agent runs:

`npx -y pushary@latest doctor`

Doctor checks every configured agent, the connection to Pushary, your key and your plan, then sends a real test push to your phone. On Windows PowerShell, type `npx.cmd -y pushary@latest doctor`. [...] `openclaw plugins inspect pushary --runtime --json npx -y pushary@latest doctor`

- `typedHooks` should list `before_tool_call`. If the plugin is missing or disabled, run `npx -y pushary@latest setup --agents openclaw`.
- Read the reason OpenClaw shows for a blocked call. It says whether the key is missing or rejected, no phone is connected, or Pushary could not be reached.
- The gateway needs the key in its own environment or in `~/.pushary/config.json`. If it runs as another user or as a service, put `PUSHARY_API_KEY` in that user's `~/.openclaw/.env` and restart the gateway.
- Only gated tools ask. By default that is every `exec` call and the `process` actions that send input to a running session; add more in `plugins.entries.pushary.config.gatedTools`. [...] ## The agent did not ask me

Fix: confirm the agent runs a Pushary hook, then check what decided the call. Run `npx -y pushary@latest doctor` and look for a failed line under that agent.
